article_title: From battlefield to community: Simulation-based education for walking blood bank whole blood transfusion.
citation: Gerhardus Christian, Bowers Alexander, Myers John C., Willis Ross, Jonas Rachelle, Manoharan Sam, Limon David, Baines Amanda M., Braverman Maxwell, Sippel Michael, Bynum James, Wampler David, Ciaraglia Angelo, Epley Sondra, Schauer Steven G., Bullock William, Eastridge Brian, Jenkins Donald, Brigmon Erika, Nicholson Susannah. (2026). From battlefield to community: Simulation‐based education for walking blood bank whole blood transfusion. Transfusion. https://doi.org/10.1111/trf.70203
title: 47-point WFWB collection and transfusion skills checklist with three sequential sections
description: A checklist of integral steps for WFWB collection and transfusion, created through literature review and iteratively revised by an expert panel of military and civilian physicians, nurses, and pre-hospital providers. "The checklist separated the procedure into three sequential sections: (1) a knowledge portion, (2) a collection portion, and (3) a transfusion portion." The maximum score is 47 points (4 for Section A, 17 for Section B, 26 for Section C).
requirements: Graders trained on the checklist and educational video by an experienced instructor to reduce interrater variability
target_learning_goals: safe collection and transfusion of warm fresh whole blood
examples: Used to grade 41 participants performing simulated WFWB collection and transfusion on a manikin model with two transfusable extremities

article_title: Exploring the dynamics of ultrasound training in medical education: current trends, debates, and approaches to didactics and hands-on learning.
citation: Recker F, Neubauer R, Dong Y, Gschmack AM, Jenssen C, Möller K, Blaivas M, Ignacio Prats M, Lucius C, Ruppert J, Sänger SL, Sirli R, Weimer J, Westerway SC, Zervides C, Dietrich CF. (2024). Exploring the dynamics of ultrasound training in medical education: current trends, debates, and approaches to didactics and hands-on learning. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-024-06092-9
title: WFUMB practical training components for undergraduate ultrasound education
description: The review enumerates the practical training components outlined in the WFUMB Position Paper Part II: "early exposure to hands-on sessions, exposure to various equipment and patient positions, training in diverse student groups, continuous assessment opportunities, structured scanning as per guidelines, and access to common pathologies relevant to the students' skill levels". It further lists mastering documentation techniques, understanding regular anatomy, and performing both fast and slow examinations as essential, with progression to supervised patient scanning and post-basic access to non-supervised skills labs. The review reports these key practical training elements substantially improved learning outcomes.
requirements: A student/teacher ratio the WFUMB recommends at 1:4, with one machine for every 4–5 students
constraints: Staff shortages and limited equipment availability constrain implementation in many clinics
target_learners: medical students in undergraduate ultrasound education
target_learning_goals: image acquisition, interpretation, documentation, and anatomy knowledge
examples: The review's abstract states key practical training elements, including early hands-on sessions and exposure to various equipment, substantially improved learning outcomes
